title: fix: accept NumPy numbers in fmt_nanoplot()

files.patch:
@@ -9486,6 +9486,15 @@ def _get_cell_y_vals(cell: Any) -> list[int | float]:
     return data_vals if isinstance(data_vals, list) else [data_vals]
 
 
+def _to_python_number(val: Any) -> Any:
+    """Turn a NumPy number (as in a pandas column) into a Python `int` or `float`."""
+
+    if val is None or isinstance(val, (int, float)):
+        return val
+
+    return val.item() if hasattr(val, "item") else float(val)
+
+
 def _generate_data_vals(
     data_vals: Any, is_x_axis: bool = False
 ) -> list[float] | tuple[list[float], list[float]]:
@@ -9517,13 +9526,13 @@ def _generate_data_vals(
 
         # Check that the values within the list are numeric; missing values are allowed
         for val in data_vals:
-            if val is not None and not isinstance(val, (int, float)):
+            if val is not None and not isinstance(val, numbers.Real):
                 raise ValueError(f"The input data values must be numeric.\n\nValue received: {val}")
 
-        return data_vals
+        return [_to_python_number(val) for val in data_vals]
 
-    elif isinstance(data_vals, int) or isinstance(data_vals, float):
-        return data_vals
+    elif isinstance(data_vals, numbers.Real):
+        return _to_python_number(data_vals)
 
     elif isinstance(data_vals, Decimal):
         return float(data_vals)

@@ -214,6 +214,33 @@ def render(vals: list[str]) -> str:
     assert render(["[1, 5, 3]", "[2; 4]"]) == render(["1 5 3", "2 4"])
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", ["int64", "int32", "float32"])
+def test_generate_data_vals_numpy_scalars(dtype: str):
+    np = pytest.importorskip("numpy")
+
+    scalar = _generate_data_vals(np.dtype(dtype).type(3))
+    values = _generate_data_vals([np.dtype(dtype).type(1), None, np.dtype(dtype).type(3)])
+
+    assert scalar == 3 and type(scalar) in (int, float)
+    assert values == [1, None, 3] and all(type(v) in (int, float) for v in values if v is not None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", ["int64", "int32", "float32"])
+def test_fmt_nanoplot_pandas_numpy_columns(dtype: str):
+    pd = pytest.importorskip("pandas")
+
+    pl_dtypes = {"int64": pl.Int64, "int32": pl.Int32, "float32": pl.Float32}
+    values = [1, 2, 3]
+    gt_pandas = GT(pd.DataFrame({"x": pd.Series(values, dtype=dtype)}), id="t").fmt_nanoplot("x")
+    gt_polars = GT(
+        pl.DataFrame({"x": pl.Series(values, dtype=pl_dtypes[dtype])}), id="t"
+    ).fmt_nanoplot("x")
+
+    # The nanoplots of a pandas column match those of a Polars column of the same dtype
+    assert gt_pandas.as_raw_html().count("<svg") == 3
+    assert gt_pandas.as_raw_html() == gt_polars.as_raw_html()
+
